pieces.title: The 60-day wait
pieces.insight: Invoicing late is a loan to your client
pieces.hook: Your client is borrowing 60 days of your payroll.
pieces.angle: Invoicing at the end of a project is a free loan to the client, and the split ends it.
pieces.verdict: A number every studio owner can check against their own month, and a fix they can use on Monday.
pieces.speaker: Dana Lee
pieces.icp_pain: We're busy and still broke at the end of the month.
pieces.outline:
Slide 1, story cover: Your client is borrowing 60 days of your payroll
Slide 2, story: most studios invoice when the project ends
Slide 3, story: four weeks of work plus net 30 plus a late payment is about 60 days
Slide 4, story: for those 60 days you pay the team, the rent and the software
Slide 5, story: the three-payment split
Slide 6, story: put it in the proposal before anyone signs
Slide 7, story: Priya's result, first third within a week
Slide 8, outro
design: Story format; the 60 days is the one yellow moment on the cover (00:24).

pieces.title: Three payments, one habit
pieces.insight: Invoicing late is a loan to your client
pieces.hook: Send the first invoice the day the work starts.
pieces.angle: The three-payment split turns a 60-day wait into cash in the first week.
pieces.verdict: Steps people will save and copy into their next proposal.
pieces.speaker: Dana Lee
pieces.quote: Send the invoice the day the work starts.
pieces.icp_pain: I check the bank balance before I check email.
